name: Visual Studio Code
summary: Microsoft's editor. The source code is MIT-licensed, but the download from Microsoft is a proprietary build with telemetry, and its extension marketplace and several key extensions are licensed only for Microsoft's own products.

factors: Marketplace terms restrict its extensions to Microsoft's own builds
Proprietary extensions with no open equivalent of the same quality: Pylance, C# Dev Kit, Remote Development, Live Share
Settings Sync through a Microsoft or GitHub account

export.summary: Settings are JSON files in your profile, and your list of extensions is one command away.

methods.name: Copy your user settings
methods.detail: settings.json, keybindings.json and the snippets folder live in the Code/User directory of your profile. Copy them to the new editor's equivalent directory.

methods.name: List your extensions
methods.detail: Run code --list-extensions to produce a list that you can reinstall from another registry.

caveats: Settings Sync data cannot be pointed at another editor; make sure the local files are current first
Check each extension's licence: some forbid use outside Microsoft's builds

paths.verdict: The same editor, built without Microsoft's branding and telemetry. Check first whether you depend on an extension that only works in Microsoft's build.

import.summary: Copy your user settings into VSCodium's profile directory and reinstall extensions from Open VSX. Most are there under the same name; check the Microsoft-proprietary ones for open replacements first.

lost: Pylance, C# Dev Kit, Live Share and Microsoft's Remote Development extensions
Extensions published only on Microsoft's Marketplace

paths.verdict: For people who want a faster editor and are open to changing their extension setup.

import.summary: Zed offers to import VS Code settings and keybindings on first run, and has a VS Code keymap. Extensions do not transfer: check that your languages and tools are covered natively or in Zed's own catalogue.

transfers: Language support through the same language servers
Git, debugging and remote development, built in
lost: Notebook and niche-language tooling that only exists as VS Code extensions
Tasks and launch configurations, which need converting
